rationale: Round 1 compiled and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this candidate raises aggressiveness while keeping risk tolerances low. The health benchmark is dominated by pointer-chasing recursive structures (trees in sim/alloc_tree, linked lists in list.c) and heavy use of shared globals, so FLA is weighted highest to flatten the state-machine-like sim loop and obscure control topology, and IGV is weighted high to globalize and hide variable provenance across the tightly coupled files. BCF stays strong but with a trimmed RuntimeCost tolerance since health's traversal loops are hot; SPLIT and SUB are cheap, low-risk multipliers applied broadly to fragment and diversify the many small functions (median function is well under 250 bytes), which also improves the effectiveness of FLA and BCF. IBR and ICALL get moderate-to-high weights to indirect branches and dispatch through the recursive/list code without the call-heavy program incurring excessive indirect-call overhead; CorrectnessRisk weights remain uniformly low to preserve the correctness the previous round demonstrated.
